title: QualityGate
description: The tenant's quality gate: the checks every vulnetix scan in CI must pass. When a check is set here it overrides the matching scan flag; a check left out leaves the flag in charge. One per tenant.

severity.description: Fail on any affected vulnerability at or above this severity. Overrides --severity.

exploits.description: Fail on a vulnerability with an exploit at or beyond this maturity. Overrides --exploits.

blockMalware.description: Fail when a dependency is known malware. Overrides --block-malware.

blockUnpinned.description: Fail on a dependency declared without a pinned version. Overrides --block-unpinned.

cooldownDays.description: Fail on a dependency version published fewer than this many days ago. Overrides --cooldown.

versionLag.description: Fail on a dependency whose installed version is among this many most recently published versions of its package: 1 fails on the newest release, 3 on any of the three newest. It holds back releases too fresh to trust, and is not a check for being out of date. 0 turns it off. Overrides --version-lag.

eol.description: End-of-life policy. A dependency whose product reaches end of life inside a horizon is reported at that horizon's severity; skip reports nothing for that horizon.

block.description: Fail the scan on end-of-life dependencies. Overrides --block-eol. It decides only whether the CLI fails: once a tenant has any stored quality gate, the server writes an end-of-life finding at the horizon severity for every scanned dependency that reaches end of life inside a horizon not set to skip, whatever this says. The CLI reads the horizon severities only when this, or --block-eol, is true.

severities.description: The severity given to a dependency by how close its end of life is. skip ignores that horizon.

scaAutofix.description: How vulnetix fix and scan --sca-autofix choose a target version.

strategy.description: latest: the newest release. safest: the release with the fewest known vulnerabilities. stable: the newest release past its cooldown. rolling: the newest release that is not malware, known vulnerabilities allowed.

maxMajorBump.description: The most major versions a fix may cross: 0 keeps fixes within the current major, N allows up to N. Any whole number from 0 up, with no upper limit. The --sca-autofix-max-major-bump flag also takes a negative number for no limit, but the gate cannot store one, and a value set here overrides the flag, so a tenant that wants no limit leaves this out.
